headline: High: Airbyte can feed Dexter shared business/financial data into broad networked APIs, creating default leakage and cascading-error risks; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented, so prompt injection is not default. However, Airbyte can move business data into files/APIs and Dexter reads from a scratchpad plus multiple APIs, so a manual or filesystem bridge could carry attacker-controlled content. The pathway is plausible but unusual and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is copied into Dexter's .dexter/scratchpad/ or another shared file
IF Dexter treats that file content as instruction-bearing text without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of generated content into Dexter scratchpads
Add a provenance header to any transferred file
Review scratchpad contents before each Dexter run

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; Dexter touches financial and market data, uses multiple third-party APIs, and handles several API keys. In default use, either agent can move sensitive data off-host, and pairing them increases the chance that one agent's outputs or inputs expose the other's data classes to external services.
conditions: IF Airbyte ingests business data that includes secrets or regulated records
IF Dexter sends scratchpad or retrieved context to OpenAI, Exa, Tavily, or Financial Datasets APIs
mitigations: Use separate API credentials per agent
Restrict both agents to redacted datasets
Block outbound traffic except approved endpoints
Disable sharing of raw files between agents
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before any API call

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and Dexter supports multiple instances plus file-based scratchpad state. Airbyte's API-driven integration work can overlap with Dexter's API-heavy research workflow, so concurrent writes or shared mutable resources could conflict if they target the same workspace or credentials. The profiles do not prove a shared directory, so this is not high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path or shared credential store
IF Airbyte and Dexter are run concurrently against the same mutable API-backed resource
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories
Use separate credential stores
Serialize runs against shared resources
Lock shared files during writes
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutexes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce transformed business data, and Dexter is an autonomous research agent that calls external APIs. If Dexter consumes Airbyte output as authoritative without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream research outputs or actions. The pair does not show direct action authority, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Dexter ingests Airbyte-produced records as ground truth
IF Dexter uses those records to generate reports or API queries without validation
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require source citations for every transferred fact
Compare outputs against original upstream records
Limit Dexter to read-only analysis of Airbyte exports
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data, while Dexter touches financial and market data and sends requests to multiple third-party APIs. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if the same regulated dataset is routed through both systems, especially because Dexter handles many API keys and external services. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated business or financial data is routed through both agents
IF either agent logs or retains that data longer than the other
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent
Avoid sending regulated data to third-party APIs
Set short retention windows for scratchpads and exports
Document which datasets each agent may process
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls
